newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai banks non-performing loans at 7.73 pct - BOT.
newsitem.headline: Thai banks non-performing loans at 7.73 pct - BOT.

text.p: The Bank of Thailand (BOT) on Friday tried to allay stock market concerns about non-performing loans of Thai commercial banks, saying they averaged only 7.73 percent of outstanding loans at end-June.

Thirachai Phuvanardnaranubal, director of the bank's supervision and development of financial institutions, said the non-performing loan figure was the average posted by 14 Thai banks, excluding the ailing Bangkok Bank of Commerce Plc which the government took over last May.
"The figure does not warrant concern, although it is at a level that the central bank should monitor and try to ease. I don't think the non-performing loans would seriously hurt Thai banks," he said.

Thailand's stock market has plummeted to over four-year lows amid foreign selling on concerns about Thai bank's loan quality, especially money lent to the depressed property sector, and some other negative factors.
On Friday the market index closed at 816.79 points, the lowest finish since September 16, 1992.

Thirachai said the 7.73 percent non-performing loan figure, up from 6.92 at end-1995, was moderate compared with 8.2 percent registered by Malaysian banks and 11.2 percent by their Indonesian counterparts.
He said the average non-performing loans of the six top Thai banks stood lower at 6.98 percent of their outstanding credits at end-June, up from 6.14 at end-1995.
He believed the Thai economic slowdown this year may have bottomed out and should improve next year.

"I believe the non-performing loan level may have peaked in June and any further rise in December would be minimal," Thirachai said, adding that the slightly higher figure this year was a product of the economic slowdown.
Thai bank stocks took a heavy beating this week on market concerns about soured property loans extended by the sector. The bank sector lost 2.85 percent on Friday.
The bank sectorial sub-index has declined 14.5 percent this month against a 11.8 percent loss for the overall market.
